turns.text: That sounds interesting! While I haven't come across that specific instance, it's not far-fetched. In classical conditioning, you pair a neutral stimulus (like the sound of the All Blacks playing) with an unconditioned stimulus (like food). Over time, the neutral stimulus alone can trigger a conditioned response, such as salivation or excitement. If the kiwi birds learned to associate the All Blacks' sound with food, they might start reacting positively to it even without the presence of the actual food.
